h1: Kepler Residence Bangkok — a serviced apartment on Soi Soonvijai that's a hundred metres from Bangkok Hospital, with full kitchens, a pool and free parking
intro: If you are coming to Bangkok for treatment at Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) on Soi Soonvijai, or accompanying a family member staying there, having a place where you can walk out of the lobby and be at the hospital entrance in under two minutes takes a real weight off the trip — Kepler Residence Bangkok sits at 11/99 Soi Phetchaburi 47 (widely known as Soi Soonvijai), roughly 100 m from Bangkok Hospital, about a 2-minute walk · What guests mention most in real reviews is the exceptional proximity to the hospital, spacious suites with full kitchens, the quiet neighbourhood, and the free parking — details that matter a great deal on a medical-travel trip · 36 suites, from about THB 2,800/night, scored 8.4 from guest reviews

body.html: Overview — who this place is for — Kepler Residence Bangkok is not a city-centre hotel for tourists who want to hop on the BTS every morning, and it doesn't try to be. It is a serviced apartment for people with a clear reason to be on Soi Soonvijai: a patient at Bangkok Hospital (BDMS), a relative staying close during treatment, a business traveller needing a proper apartment for several weeks, or a family that arrives by car and wants space plus a kitchen. The single most important number is 100 metres — roughly a 2-minute walk from the lobby to the hospital entrance, as multiple guests confirm in their reviews. The property opened in 2017 and was renovated in 2018, and the consensus from real reviews is that it earns its 8.4 score for guests using it as intended: hospital proximity + spacious kitchen suite + free parking + quiet surroundings.

Location and getting around — The address is 11/99 Soi Phetchaburi 47 (Soi Soonvijai), Bang Kapi, Huai Khwang, Bangkok 10310. The defining feature is the distance to Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) Soonvijai branch: approximately 100 m, under 2 minutes on foot — mentioned in virtually every positive review. For public transport: ARL Makkasan (Airport Rail Link to Suvarnabhumi) is about 1.1 km away, roughly a 12–15 min walk or a short Grab ride, which makes airport transfers practical and affordable. MRT Phetchaburi is around 1.5 km, or 18–20 minutes walking — realistic by Grab rather than on foot in Bangkok's heat. There is no BTS or MRT within a 10-minute walk, so guests who plan to rely on the rail network every day will find this neighbourhood inconvenient. Several reviews describe the area as feeling 'remote' or 'secluded', which is accurate — but for those who need to be close to Bangkok Hospital, that quiet, off-the-main-road setting is exactly what they are looking for.
"The room is spacious and very close to Bangkok Hospital — 2 minutes walk. Staff were very helpful and the free parking made everything easy."

Room types and space — There are 36 suites divided into four types. Deluxe King Suite: one king bed, full kitchen, washer/dryer, balcony — the entry-level option, well suited to a solo patient or a couple. Grand Deluxe Twin Suite: two single beds, the practical choice for a patient and a companion sharing a room. Grand Deluxe King Suite: king bed with a sofa bed, more floor space. Family Two Bedrooms Suite: two bedrooms (one double, two singles), the best option for families or groups who need separate sleeping areas. Every suite comes with a refrigerator, stovetop, microwave, washer/dryer and a dining area — the kind of kit that makes a week-long stay genuinely comfortable and cuts down on meal costs. Guests consistently praise the spaciousness and quietness, thanks to the property sitting off the main road in a side soi. One honest caveat that appears in a TripAdvisor review: some furniture shows its age, which is not surprising for a property that opened in 2017 — worth bearing in mind if you are expecting showroom-fresh interiors.

Facilities — The property offers an outdoor swimming pool open from 06:00 to 22:00, with a children's pool and hot tub alongside, good for unwinding after a long hospital day. There is a gym with up-to-date equipment and a massage room for anyone who needs to look after themselves during a longer stay. The on-site restaurant and snack bar covers basic meals. Free private parking is one of the most-praised practical details — finding safe, free parking in Bangkok is not easy, and it removes a genuine hassle for guests arriving by car. Wi-Fi is free throughout. One important thing to note upfront: breakfast is not included in any room type, which a few reviews mention catching them off guard. Every suite has a full kitchen, so cooking your own breakfast is the intended solution.

What guests actually say — the good and the honest — Drawing from reviews on Trip.com, Booking.com, Agoda and TripAdvisor, the picture is fairly consistent. Positive highlights: the 2-minute walk to Bangkok Hospital comes up in nearly every review without exception; spacious suites with functional kitchens get specific praise from guests on longer stays; the quiet backstreet setting away from traffic noise is appreciated; free parking is mentioned as a genuine bonus; and staff are described as friendly, with English and Arabic service both noted. Points to consider honestly: the location is genuinely far from the BTS and MRT, so anyone who wants to explore Bangkok easily will need to budget for Grab rides every time; there is no breakfast service, which some guests did not expect; one TripAdvisor reviewer described cleanliness as 'superficial' and the apartment as 'a little small for 4 people', though this sits against mostly positive scores on other platforms; and a small number of reviews mention a faint smell of smoke in certain areas. The overall picture is that this property works very well for its target guest and less well for general sightseeing trips.
"Convenient location less than a 5-minute walk from the hospital. Comfortable beds. If you're not looking for 4-star comfort in every detail, it does the job well — especially for medical visits."

Price and value — Rooms start from approximately THB 2,800–3,200/night for a Deluxe King Suite in standard season (around USD$79–95 as shown on Agoda and Kayak), rising to roughly THB 3,800–4,500+ during peak periods or public holidays. The Family Two Bedrooms Suite is priced higher in proportion to its size. For the intended use case, the value calculation is straightforward: a kitchen-equipped suite with free parking, a pool and a 2-minute walk to Bangkok Hospital at that price point competes well against alternatives in the area. When you factor in savings on restaurant meals (the kitchen handles that), saved Grab costs (you walk to the hospital instead of riding), and the peace of mind of being steps away from the hospital, the nightly rate often works out well. For pure sightseeing tourism, equally priced hotels near BTS stations in Ratchathewi or Siam will serve you better.

What to know before booking — First: no breakfast is included in any room type, full stop — the kitchen in each suite is the answer for self-catering, or there are cafes and convenience stores a short walk away in the soi. Second: this neighbourhood requires Grab or a car for most outings; MRT Phetchaburi is 1.5 km and not practical to walk in the heat. Third: if you need to reach Suvarnabhumi Airport, ARL Makkasan is about 1.1 km away — a short Grab ride puts you on the Airport Rail Link, which is far cheaper than a taxi from the property. Fourth: if you are sensitive to smoke smells, mention your preference when booking, as a few guests have flagged this. Fifth: rooms near Bangkok Hospital tend to fill quickly in hospital-visit peak periods (early January and around year-end); book in advance and choose free cancellation to stay flexible if medical dates shift.

Bottom line — Kepler Residence Bangkok earns its place as one of the closest serviced apartments to Bangkok Hospital (BDMS) Soonvijai branch. For patients, carers, or anyone needing to live conveniently near that hospital, the combination of a 100 m walk to the hospital, full-kitchen suites, free parking and a decent pool at around THB 2,800+ a night is hard to beat in this area. If you are coming to Bangkok to sightsee and want easy BTS access, Ratchathewi or Siam will suit you better. But if proximity to Bangkok Hospital is your priority — Kepler Residence Bangkok is the clearest answer in the neighbourhood.

faqTitle: Kepler Residence Bangkok — Frequently Asked Questions

faq.q: How far is Kepler Residence Bangkok from Bangkok Hospital (BDMS)?
faq.a: Approximately 100 metres — under a 2-minute walk from the lobby to the hospital entrance. This is the most-mentioned detail across all guest reviews and is the property's defining location advantage.

faq.q: Is Kepler Residence Bangkok close to an MRT or BTS station?
faq.a: MRT Phetchaburi is about 1.5 km away (around 18–20 min walk, more practical by Grab) and ARL Makkasan is about 1.1 km away (12–15 min walk or a very short Grab ride). There is no BTS or MRT within easy walking distance, so guests relying on rail for daily city travel should be aware of this.

faq.q: Does Kepler Residence Bangkok include breakfast?
faq.a: No breakfast is included in any room type. Every suite has a full kitchen (fridge, stovetop, microwave) so self-catering is easy, and there are small cafes and convenience stores a short walk away in the soi.

faq.q: Is parking free at Kepler Residence Bangkok?
faq.a: Yes — free private parking is available for all guests. This is a meaningful practical advantage given how difficult free parking can be to find in Bangkok, and is particularly useful for families or medical-travel guests arriving by car.

faq.q: Who is Kepler Residence Bangkok best suited for?
faq.a: It is best suited to patients at Bangkok Hospital BDMS, companions or carers staying nearby, and longer-stay business travellers or families arriving by car who want spacious kitchen suites and free parking. It is not well suited to tourists who want to explore Bangkok by rail every day — for that, a hotel near a BTS or MRT station in Ratchathewi, Siam or Sukhumvit is a better fit.
